children: The motorcycle maker's seven-year investment plan will add to its existing electric mobility and manufacturing footprint in the state

Royal Enfield is stepping up its electric mobility ambitions with a proposed Rs 1,000 crore investment in Tamil Nadu over the next seven years. The company has entered into a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the state government to strengthen its electric vehicle (EV) capabilities.

The proposed capital deployment will cover EV development, technology and manufacturing, while creating direct and indirect employment for up to 500 people. The investment gives Royal Enfield a longer-term manufacturing and technology roadmap for electric motorcycles in one of its key production bases.

On this development, B. Govindarajan, Managing Director, Eicher Motors and CEO, Royal Enfield, said, "Tamil Nadu has been our home and the anchor for our engineering and manufacturing for several decades. This investment underscores our enduring commitment to the state, its world-class automotive ecosystem, and our vision for the future of electric mobility. We extend our sincere gratitude to the Government of Tamil

Nadu for its continued support. As we expand our EV capabilities, we remain focused on creating a positive impact for the local community and delivering authentic motorcycles that are Made in Chennai and celebrated across the world."

Royal Enfield's electric strategy is being developed under Flying Flea, its electric mobility brand. The company has an EV innovation laboratory and manufacturing facility at Vallam Vadagal in Tamil Nadu, giving the state a central role in its electric motorcycle plans.

The EV investment comes against the backdrop of a wider manufacturing expansion by Royal Enfield's parent, Eicher Motors, in Tamil Nadu. In February 2026, the company committed Rs 958 crore towards expanding capacity at its Cheyyar facility. That project is expected to take Eicher Motors' total annual motorcycle production capacity to 2 million units.

The latest commitment is distinct from the Cheyyar expansion, with the new investment directed towards the company's electric mobility ecosystem. Together, the two initiatives point to a broader effort to build both conventional and emerging motorcycle manufacturing capabilities in the state. Tamil Nadu currently houses four Royal Enfield manufacturing facilities, besides the company's head office and technical centre.
The company has maintained a long-standing investment relationship with the state, with Eicher Motors having signed earlier MoUs with the Tamil Nadu government in 2012, 2019 and 2024.
